justifications.functional_suitability: All requirements are fulfilled: R-01 via 'SFU Media Server / LiveKit' and 'Consultation Manager', R-02 via 'US FHIR Adapter' and 'EU E-Prescription Gateway', R-03 via 'AI Inference Wrapper', and R-04 via 'Consent & Policy Engine' and client-side 'Consent Enforcement Component'.
justifications.performance_efficiency: Adaptive bitrate streaming in 'WebRTC Client Component' and 'SFU Media Server', gRPC for internal communications, and async dispatch via Pub/Sub support performance targets. However, concrete caching strategies for database reads or AI inference are not explicitly defined.
justifications.compatibility: R-08 is addressed thoroughly via 'US FHIR Adapter' using 'FHIR Mapping Engine' for HL7 FHIR, alongside 'EU E-Prescription Gateway' featuring 'National Adapter Engine' supporting mTLS, SOAP, and REST for national EU gateways.
justifications.usability: Both 'Patients & Clinicians' access the system through 'Single-Patient / Mobile App'. While Flutter provides cross-platform UI, combining distinct patient and clinician workflows into a single patient-centric mobile application leaves clinician interface needs superficially addressed.
justifications.reliability: The architecture satisfies R-06 through 'WebRTC Client Component' (degraded network recovery) and 'SFU Media Server / LiveKit'. 'Local Sync & State Management Component' supports offline-first operation, while 'Rate Limiting & Circuit Breaker' prevents systemic cascade failures.
justifications.security: Data residency is enforced by 'Regional Database Instances', 'Consent & Policy Engine', and regional adapters. Security is reinforced with 'JWT & mTLS Termination Filter', SQLCipher, customer-managed KMS keys in 'Encrypted Blob Storage', and immutable traceability in 'Audit & Compliance Ledger'.
justifications.maintainability: Decomposition is clean and modular. Decoupling region-specific logic into 'US FHIR Adapter' and 'EU E-Prescription Gateway' isolates regulatory changes, while the 'AI Inference Wrapper' cleanly isolates model integration and versioning from core business logic.
justifications.portability: The architecture deploys cleanly across the required GCP regions (europe-west3 and us-central1) using containerized services on GKE. However, reliance on proprietary services like Cloud SQL, Cloud KMS, and Cloud Storage creates minor vendor lock-in for non-GCP environments.

PERF-01.justification: LiveKit SFU on GKE with adaptive bitrate and Go-based core services handle high concurrency well. However, auto-scaling details and TURN server capacity planning under 5,000 concurrent media sessions are not explicitly detailed.
sensitivity_points: GKE cluster scaling speed and SFU bandwidth capacity
TURN/ICE relay capacity during network fallback
tradeoffs: Lower media resolution under load preserves session stability over fidelity

PERF-02.justification: FastAPI wrapper, Pub/Sub asynchronous logging, and rate limiting support high throughput. The ~14 req/s load is manageable, though upstream AI latency depends heavily on model deployment infrastructure.
sensitivity_points: AI inference backend execution time and queue depth
Async audit dispatch throughput via Pub/Sub
tradeoffs: Asynchronous audit logging improves response times but risks slight telemetry delay

AVAIL-01.justification: LiveKit client/SFU supports adaptive bitrate down to audio-only. Mobile app has offline-first local caching (SQLCipher/Hive) ensuring clinical notes and consultation state are preserved during severe degradation.
sensitivity_points: Adaptive bitrate threshold tuning for 200 kbit/s streams
tradeoffs: Dropping video track guarantees uninterrupted audio and persistent note sync

AVAIL-02.justification: Regional database instances are deployed strictly in us-central1 and europe-west3, but no secondary US region, cross-zone failover, or disaster recovery strategy is defined to restore service within 1 hour without moving data.
sensitivity_points: Multi-zone or multi-region intra-US failover configuration
Recovery Time Objective (RTO) without cross-border replication
tradeoffs: Strict regional data confinement prevents cross-border failover, reducing disaster recovery options

MOD-01.justification: The EU E-Prescription Gateway explicitly encapsulates a pluggable National Adapter Engine using Spring Integration, allowing additions of national standards without affecting core telehealth services.
sensitivity_points: Standardization of internal interfaces in the National Adapter Engine
Decoupling of national transport protocols from core prescription logic
tradeoffs: Modular adapter abstraction increases code surface but isolates country-specific maintenance

MOD-02.justification: The AI Inference Wrapper and Core Telehealth Service include dedicated Model Client Adapters and Audit & Traceability Loggers that specifically record model versioning, inputs, and outputs immutably into PostgreSQL ledger tables.
sensitivity_points: Strict semantic model version tagging in inference payloads
Immutability of the Audit & Compliance Ledger
tradeoffs: Comprehensive model audit logging adds storage overhead to ensure MDR compliance

SEC-01.justification: The Consent & Policy Engine, Consent Enforcement Interceptor, and database-level RLS explicitly verify purpose-based patient consent before cross-region access, with every attempt captured in the Audit & Compliance Ledger.
sensitivity_points: Strict evaluation of dynamic consent tokens across region boundaries
Enforcement of PostgreSQL Row Level Security (RLS) policies
tradeoffs: Mandatory synchronous consent evaluation introduces minor request latency

SEC-02.justification: Consent updates are processed by the Consent & Policy Engine and stored immutably in the ledger. Interceptors enforce updated tokens immediately. However, an automated workflow to revoke access for offline research datasets is not fully specified.
sensitivity_points: Cache invalidation latency for active user consent tokens
Propagation of consent withdrawal to downstream data pipelines
tradeoffs: Real-time token revocation checks add authorization overhead to queries
